title: i18n: `i18n.defaultLocale` is both the users' default language and the authoring (source) language — an English-authored app that defaults users to zh-CN gets 446 false "missing en" lint gaps and loses its zh-CN coverage check
body:
Found by a downstream app on the published 18.4.0 packages (steedos-labs/os-project-blackcat-crm#67, PR #72).

## Symptom

The app's metadata is authored in English (inline labels), with `zh-CN` / `es-ES` / `ja-JP` packs. Setting `i18n.defaultLocale: 'zh-CN'` (so users without a personal locale, and the boot seed, get Chinese) makes `objectstack lint --strict` read the inline text as **zh-CN source**: it reports **446 `missing translation for locale "en"`** and stops seeing real zh-CN gaps (downstream ablation: removing a zh-CN account description → 0 zh-CN gaps reported). The app works around nothing in metadata but has to run `objectstack lint --strict --default-locale en` to keep its Chinese pack checked.

## Why it matters

"Which language do users get by default" and "which language is the inline metadata written in" are different facts for any app sold into a market other than its authors'. One key carrying both forces apps to either keep a wrong user default or pass a lint flag that every other reader of the setting (i18n extract / check, docs) does not know about.

## Suggested fix shape (for the lane to judge)

A separate source-language key (e.g. `i18n.sourceLocale`, defaulting to `defaultLocale` for compatibility) read by lint / `os i18n extract` / `check` as the authoring language, while `defaultLocale` stays the users' default.

Dedupe words: i18n coverage source locale · defaultLocale authoring language · lint default-locale.
